checklist.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Does compute_fork_version safely handle all epoch values from attacker-controlled ENR records?

reachability.notes: Edge case epoch values (0, max uint64) from attacker-crafted ENR records could trigger panics.

checklist.test_procedure: 1. Identify the compute_fork_version function and trace all callers from P2P entry points. 2. Review the ENR eth2 field parsing to verify epoch values are validated before being passed to compute_fork_version. 3. Craft test ENR records with edge case epoch values: 0, 1, max uint64 (18446744073709551615), and max uint64 - 1. 4. Submit these crafted ENR records via P2P and monitor for panics, exceptions, or null returns. 5. Verify the function returns a valid Version type for all inputs without crashing the node. 6. Check error handling paths to ensure graceful degradation rather than panic.
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0003, Trust Boundary: tb-009, Invariant: p2p:SG-001:INV-003. PoC approach: craft ENR record with extreme epoch value causing node crash.

checklist.title: Verify compute_fork_version maintains return type invariant across all epoch edge cases

reachability.notes: Edge case epoch values (0, max uint64) from attacker-crafted ENR records could trigger panics.

checklist.test_procedure: 1. Unit test compute_fork_version with epoch = 0 to verify valid Version returned. 2. Unit test with epoch = uint64_max (18446744073709551615) to verify no overflow/panic. 3. Test with epoch values at each fork transition boundary. 4. Verify return type is always Version (never null/nil). 5. Check for any panic-inducing code paths (unwrap, expect, assert) that could be triggered by edge case inputs. 6. Review fork configuration loading to ensure all expected fork epochs are properly defined.
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0003, Supporting check for boundary verification. Focus on internal logic ensuring the invariant holds.

checklist.title: Falsify Pre-condition: Can upgrade_to_fulu be triggered at non-epoch boundary slots?

reachability.notes: Fork trigger is an internal state transition. An attacker cannot directly invoke it, but an off-by-one error would cause a consensus split at FULU_FORK_EPOCH.

checklist.test_procedure: 1. Identify the upgrade_to_fulu function and locate the epoch boundary check (state.slot % SLOTS_PER_EPOCH == 0). 2. Verify the check uses correct SLOTS_PER_EPOCH constant (32 slots). 3. Test edge cases: slot = FULU_FORK_EPOCH * SLOTS_PER_EPOCH - 1 (should NOT trigger), slot = FULU_FORK_EPOCH * SLOTS_PER_EPOCH (should trigger), slot = FULU_FORK_EPOCH * SLOTS_PER_EPOCH + 1 (should NOT trigger). 4. Check for off-by-one errors in the modulo operation or comparison. 5. Verify no other code path can invoke upgrade_to_fulu bypassing this check. 6. Simulate state transitions at slots immediately before and after FULU_FORK_EPOCH boundary to confirm fork triggers exactly once at the correct slot.
checklist.falsification_approach: Attempt to trigger the fork state transition at a slot where state.slot % SLOTS_PER_EPOCH != 0. If successful, this would cause a network split where buggy nodes fork at incorrect slots relative to correct implementations.
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0004, Pre-condition for fork:SG-001:fork_trigger. Critical severity due to consensus split risk. Even though internal-only, explicitly in-scope for Fusaka bug bounty.

checklist.title: Falsify Fork Trigger Single-Fire Invariant: Can FULU_FORK_EPOCH trigger fire more than once or not at all during chain reorganizations?

reachability.notes: If the fork triggers multiple times (e.g., during reorg at fork epoch boundary), state corruption would occur. The guard condition must ensure idempotent single-fire.

checklist.test_procedure: 1. Identify all code paths where compute_epoch_at_slot(state.slot) == FULU_FORK_EPOCH is evaluated. 2. Trace the upgrade_to_fulu function and verify it has idempotent guards preventing re-execution on already-upgraded state. 3. Construct a reorg scenario at the fork epoch boundary where the chain rewinds to pre-fork state and advances past fork epoch again. 4. Verify the fork trigger guard checks for already-upgraded state (e.g., state version field) before executing upgrade logic. 5. Test edge case: What happens if state.slot crosses FULU_FORK_EPOCH multiple times due to reorg? Does the guard prevent double-initialization of proposer_lookahead? 6. Verify that proposer_lookahead initialization cannot corrupt an already-initialized structure if called twice. 7. Test missed trigger scenario: Simulate a node that skips the exact fork epoch slot - verify it still upgrades on the next slot. 8. Check for race conditions in concurrent state processing that could allow parallel fork triggers.
checklist.falsification_approach: Demonstrate that the fork trigger can fire more than once during a reorg at the fork epoch boundary, causing proposer_lookahead re-initialization on an already-upgraded state, OR demonstrate that the trigger can be missed entirely, causing the node to permanently fork off the network.
checklist.invariant_under_test: compute_epoch_at_slot(state.slot) == FULU_FORK_EPOCH evaluates to true exactly once during chain lifetime, and the state transition is irreversible
attack_vectors: Chain reorganization spanning the fork epoch boundary
Multiple blocks at fork epoch processed in quick succession
Node restart during fork epoch transition
Late block attestation causing reorg at boundary
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0005, Invariant: fork:SG-001:INV-002, Assumption: asm-002, Threat: stride-021, Primary Element: fork:SG-001:fork_trigger. Bug bounty eligible - demonstrate scenario where upgrade_to_fulu fires more than once or not at all.
